title: Getting started

text: ivd implements Spike--Slab Mixed-Effects Location Scale Model (SS-MELSM, Carmo et al. 2026) detect heterogeneous residual variances hierarchical data. standard mixed-effects models assume constant within-group variability, mixed-effects location scale models explicitly models residual variance function covariates random effects. MELSM approach covariance matrix (thus correlation matrix) random effects across location scale estimated jointly within likelihood. SS-MELSM uses spike--slab prior probabilistically identify specific units (e.g., schools, individuals) exhibit unusually high low consistency, distinguishing population average.

ivd() fits SS-MELSM lme4-style formulas location scale sub-models; chains run parallel, grouping IDs (character, factor, non-consecutive numeric codes) accepted. summary() plot() report unit’s posterior inclusion probability (PIP), PIP, funnel, outcome plots; results can labelled original grouping IDs (labels = "original"). pip(), fixef(), ranef(), coef() extract tidy estimates processing. pip_sensitivity() shows PIPs – resulting classifications – change different prior inclusion probabilities, computed analytically without refitting. codaplot() provides MCMC diagnostic plots readable parameter names.

X_location_names, Z_location_names: Names fixed random effects location submodel. X_scale, Z_scale: Matrices used scale submodel’s fixed random effects. Y: Data frame response vector group identifiers. group_labels: Character vector mapping internal cluster index j back user's original grouping IDs. location_formula, scale_formula: model formulas. ss_prior_p: prior inclusion probability used fit. workers: Number parallel chains used. ...: Additional elements created internally used downstream S3 methods (print(), summary(), etc.). object designed support S3 methods printing, summarizing, extracting results ivd model.

title: ivd (development version)
text: ivd() accepts arbitrary grouping IDs (character, factor, numeric gaps, e.g. real school codes). IDs recoded internally 1..J index NIMBLE needs – without reordering data – original labels stored fitted object group_labels. summary() plot() gained shared labels = c("index", "original") argument: default keeps compact internal cluster index displays; "original" switches user’s grouping IDs. New print() method fitted objects: formulas, data dimensions, sampling setup, one-line convergence note (max split-Rhat, min n_eff). New pip() extractor returning posterior inclusion probabilities tidy data frame (one row per cluster x scale random effect, original cluster IDs). New fixef(), ranef(), coef() extractors following lme4/nlme conventions (without adding dependency either). New pip_sensitivity(): analytic prior-sensitivity PIPs. posterior odds converted prior-independent Bayes factor re-weighted across grid prior inclusion probabilities – refit needed. Comes plot() method showing per-cluster PIP trajectories (prior-sensitive clusters highlighted; subset clusters =). summary() now returns structured summary.ivd object ($table, $waic, $lppd, $pwaic, $chains) rendered separate print() method; console output unchanged.

title: ivd (development version)
text: Fixed crash default n_eff = "local" diagnostics short strongly autocorrelated chains (Geyer truncation empty set produced 1:Inf). .autocorrelation_fft() now actually zero-pads, computing linear rather circular autocorrelation; results match stats::acf(). Fixed row offset linking PIPs clusters summary() codaplot() models number location scale random effects differ. DESCRIPTION now correctly states spike--slab prior scale random effects, cites published paper: Carmo, Williams & Rast (2026) doi:10.3102/10769986261426004.
